en.title: How the FaMED Prep App Works: Four Practice Sections
en.excerpt: Real app screens and concrete instructions: select cases, practice conversations and written tasks, and use available feedback.
en.content:
Watch the walkthrough above, then choose one skill to practise. The four sections follow the same order here and in the video: **Anamnese → Aufklärung → Arzt–Arzt → Arztbrief**. Each section below explains the task, shows the matching app screen, and suggests how to use the feedback.

## 1. Anamnese: ask, listen and follow up

Practise a patient conversation in German. Choose an available fictional patient, read the situation, and ask your first question. The patient responds during the exercise; listen to the answer before deciding what to ask next. Follow the microphone instructions shown in your browser and exercise.

![Anamnese practice screen in the actual FaMED Prep app](/images/previews/app-anamnese-practice-20261020.png)

*Anamnese: the conversation exercise shown with a fictional patient. The sidebar is excluded so you can focus on the task.*

The video includes two scripted doctor questions with actual patient-response audio from the app. This demonstrates the exchange; it is an edited example, not a real student's attempt.

After a conversation, use the available feedback to choose your next practice goal. In the illustrated six-question demo, the Anamnese ratings were **100% grammar, 70% fluency and structure, and 100% clarity**. The comments flagged a repeated question. These are ratings of the transcript, not a measurement of vocal intonation or an official exam score.

**Try this:** ask about the main complaint, then ask a follow-up based on something the patient has just told you. Avoid repeating a question that has already been answered.

## 2. Aufklärung: explain a procedure to the patient

Choose a procedure and read your role, the fictional case and the instructions. Practise explaining the planned procedure in language a patient can understand. Organise the explanation and leave room for questions.

![Aufklärung task showing the role, scenario and instructions](/images/previews/app-aufklaerung-task-20261020.png)

*Aufklärung: read this task before recording your explanation. This screenshot previews the task; it does not show a completed assessment.*

Full-test feedback separates **Inhalt, Struktur and Grammatik**: what you included, how you organised the explanation, and which language points need attention. Read the comments and repeat one part of your explanation with a specific improvement.

**Try this:** introduce the procedure in two clear sentences, then explain one relevant risk in patient-friendly language. Our [Aufklärung practice guide](/blog/famed-aufklaerungsgespraech-guide) gives you a starting structure.

## 3. Arzt–Arzt: present the case to a colleague

Select an available handover case, then read the patient information and your task. Decide which facts matter for the colleague who will receive the handover. Practise presenting the case in a clear order, including your assessment and proposed next steps where the task asks for them.

![Arzt–Arzt case information and handover task](/images/previews/app-handover-task-20261020.png)

*Arzt–Arzt: the actual handover task, with the sidebar hidden. The case is fictional.*

The full test gives feedback on **Struktur, Inhalt, Sprachliche Präzision and Kommunikationsstil**. Use the comments to make the next presentation clearer and more focused.

**Try this:** give a short opening summary before adding details. If you need a framework, use our [SBAR practice guide](/blog/sbar-schema-arzt-arzt-gespraech).

## 4. Arztbrief: listen, write and review

Open an available writing exercise and listen to the practice recording. Work through the information in a sensible order, write your own answer, and submit it for AI practice feedback. The video includes an audible excerpt from the actual exercise and sequential typing in the app.

![Answer being typed in the actual Arztbrief exercise](/images/previews/app-writing-20261020.png)

*Arztbrief: actual typing using a demo account and a fictional case. This is an example answer, not a model answer to memorise.*

Review **Struktur, Vollständigkeit, Fachterminologie, Grammatik and Präzision**. Choose one useful correction from the specific comments and apply it in the next attempt.

**Try this:** practise one manageable section before writing the complete account. Our [Arztbrief writing guide](/blog/famed-arztbrief-soap-schema) can help you plan the structure.

## Build a practice routine you can repeat

Choose one section, complete one task, and carry one useful correction into your next attempt. Use the [30-minute routine](/blog/famed-vorbereitung-30-minuten-lernroutine) or [eight-week study plan](/blog/8-week-famed-study-plan) to organise your week.

Practice tasks and exam simulations have different access rules and limits. Check the current [plan overview](https://famedtestprep.com/Upgrade?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=walkthrough&utm_campaign=app_plans) before choosing access. AI feedback supports preparation; it does not replace your examination provider's requirements.

## Choose your next step

[Explore available app tasks](https://famedtestprep.com/MedicalCases?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=walkthrough&utm_campaign=app_intro). One-month app access is **€25.99 for 30 days**; available tasks and limits depend on the plan.

Prefer to start with reading? The digital casebook is **€19.99**. [Read a real book preview](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau). An optional **€59.99 package** combines the digital book with 90 days of app access; [view its details](https://famedtestprep.com/PayPalCheckout?plan=bundle_3m&utm_source=blog&utm_medium=walkthrough&utm_campaign=optional_bundle).

en.title: FaMED Preparation: A 30-Minute Daily Study Routine
en.excerpt: A concrete daily exercise: structure a conversation, formulate it aloud, check feedback, and practice the same section again.
en.content:
You've collected study material, but are you also practicing speaking? For preparing for medical language situations, a fixed workflow helps. Here is a 30-minute routine that you can adapt to your learning level. This is a learning suggestion from FaMED Prep, not an official exam requirement and no guarantee of passing.

## Minutes 0–5: One Learning Goal Instead of Ten Topics

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

Choose a single task: open a conversation, summarize information, or formulate a section of a doctor's letter. Write down what you want to express more clearly at the end. Example: "Today I will practice politely asking for clarification on an unclear answer."


If you want to continue practicing this topic, also read [Mastering the FaMED Anamnese: Part 1 - Overview & Key Strategies](/blog/anamnese-overview-part-1).


Do you first need a schedule for your study weeks? [You can find the free study plan here](/lead-magnet).

## Minutes 5–15: Practice Aloud

Speak the task aloud. Record yourself with your own device or practice with a study partner. Use a case example, but do not memorize a supposedly universal model answer. Your formulations should fit the specific situation.

If you are missing a word, mark the spot and continue speaking. This way, you will notice which gaps actually hinder you in conversation.


## Minutes 15–20: Three Concrete Observations

Listen to your recording. Note only three things: Was the sequence understandable? Were your sentences clear? Which part do you want to formulate more precisely? For medical content, you need a professionally appropriate source or qualified feedback; language training does not replace this review.


For the next learning step, [How to Prepare for the FaMED Exam While Working Full-Time (6-Week Plan)](/blog/famed-vorbereitung-berufstaetig-6-wochen) will help you.

## Minutes 20–27: Repeat the Difficult Section

Practice the same section again. Change a formulation and compare both attempts. The goal is a noticeable improvement instead of an ever-longer list of unread materials.


Do you want to not just read, but practice practically? [Here we show the FaMED Prep App step by step](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts) before you decide on access.

## Minutes 27–30: Note the Next Step

Write down one sentence: "Tomorrow I will repeat...". Keep your notes and check after a week which tasks are easier for you. As your exam date approaches, align your overall plan with your individual needs and the current information from the respective exam provider.

## How to Combine Reading and Practicing

You can use the digital FaMED Protocol casebook for reference; in the FaMED Prep App, you can practically work through the available exercises. The package includes the digital book and **90 days of app access for a total price of €59.99, one-time**. The respective plan limits are in the app; there is no promise of an unlimited number of exam simulations.

[View Digital Book + 90 Days App for €59.99](https://famedtestprep.com/PayPalCheckout?plan=bundle_3m&utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=30min_routine)

Do you want an overview first? [Here you will find our free study plan](/lead-magnet). Also check the current information from your exam provider: [FaMed](https://famed-test.de/).

en.title: FaMED Aufklärung: Explain the Supplied Procedure Clearly
en.excerpt: Explain the supplied procedure in everyday German, discuss risks honestly and respond to patient questions.
en.content:
In the human-medicine FaMed format, informed consent is one situation in the doctor–patient station. The current practice test allows **at most 11 minutes** for the situation; the paired oral block lasts **23 minutes including reading**.

The necessary procedure information is supplied. Your job is to explain it clearly, respond to questions and check understanding. Medical knowledge is not separately assessed. A memorised procedure script must not override the assignment.

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

## 1. Establish the topic and purpose

Introduce yourself, check whom you are speaking with and state the planned procedure in everyday language. Do not assume this person is the patient from the preceding history task.

> Wir sprechen heute über die geplante Untersuchung. Ich erkläre Ihnen den Anlass, den Ablauf, mögliche Risiken und was davor und danach wichtig ist. Welche Frage haben Sie zunächst?

Use the actual indication from the material. Do not invent urgency or say the procedure is compulsory.

## 2. Explain the sequence

Turn the supplied steps into a short, chronological explanation. Translate a technical term when needed. If a possible additional step is described, preserve that uncertainty rather than saying it will definitely happen.

For a language exercise: „Gewebeprobe“ can become „eine kleine Probe aus dem Gewebe, die anschließend untersucht wird“. Whether a sample is planned in a particular case must come from its information.

## 3. Communicate risks honestly

Explain the listed general and specific risks without minimising or exaggerating them. Use a numerical frequency only when supported by the task or a suitable current clinical source. This article does not provide a complete procedure-specific consent checklist.

A better language pattern is:

> Ich verstehe Ihre Sorge. Ich erkläre Ihnen, welches Risiko hier beschrieben wird und welche Maßnahmen vorgesehen sind. Welche Information würde Ihnen bei der Entscheidung helfen?

## 4. Cover preparation and aftercare from the material

Explain the supplied instructions about eating, medication, activity or follow-up. Do not invent a universal fasting period, driving ban or bed-rest rule for every intervention. These depend on the actual procedure, sedation and clinical instructions.

## 5. Make room for questions and a decision

Ask the person to explain the key point in their own words. Respond to their concern, then return to the structure. Respect uncertainty or refusal; do not use a dramatic consequence that is not supported by the case.

For further practice, use [everyday-language terminology](/blog/medizinische-fachbegriffe-laiensprache-tabelle) and [patient idioms](/blog/deutsche-patientensprache-redewendungen). The [book sample](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau) and [app walkthrough](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts) show optional independent learning resources. We have not verified a ranking of the seven most frequent official procedures.

## Sources and review

Editorial check: **18 October 2026**, human medicine. [Exam flow](https://famed-test.de/pruefungsablauf/), [Practice test](https://famed-test.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/FaMed-Uebungstest_2-1.pdf), [IQWiG: lumbar puncture](https://www.gesundheitsinformation.de/was-passiert-bei-einer-lumbalpunktion.html), [DGN guideline, March2026](https://register.awmf.org/assets/guidelines/030-141l_S1_Lumbalpunktion-Liquordiagnostik_2026-03.pdf). Practice examples are created by FaMED Prep; they are not predictions of exam questions.

en.title: FaMED Patient Presentations: Use SBAR as a Practice Framework
en.excerpt: Organise two separate case presentations from supplied information, without inventing findings or treating SBAR as the official rubric.
en.content:
The doctor–doctor station contains **two patient presentations**. Its published duration is **23 minutes including reading**; the current practice test allows **at most 11 minutes per situation**. The cases need to be kept separate.

You communicate relevant supplied information in professional German and answer follow-up questions. This is a language task, not a requirement to recall a treatment algorithm from memory.

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

## SBAR is an organising tool

SBAR can give a practice presentation a clear route. It is not the official mandatory answer template or a numerical scoring rubric.

| Part | Useful question |
|---|---|
| Situation | Who is being presented, and why? |
| Background | Which reported symptoms and history matter? |
| Assessment | Which findings and interpretation are actually supplied? |
| Recommendation | What course, plan or requested next step belongs to this task? |

A supplied case can call for a different emphasis. Do not force information into an empty category.

## A short fictional source-to-speech exercise

Practice notes: Frau Beispiel, 54; cough for five days; no temperature value supplied; medication list available in the task; examination report not supplied.

A faithful opening might be:

> Ich stelle Frau Beispiel, eine 54-jährige Patientin, vor. Sie berichte über seit fünf Tagen bestehenden Husten. Eine gemessene Temperatur ist in den vorliegenden Angaben nicht dokumentiert.

This is deliberately a short language exercise. It does not support adding normal vital signs, prescribing medication or announcing a diagnosis.

## Respond to a follow-up precisely

If asked about information that is present, answer briefly and accurately. If it is missing, say so:

> Dazu liegen mir in der Aufgabeninformation keine Angaben vor.

Distinguish „bereits durchgeführt“, „geplant“ and „von mir vorgeschlagen“. Never turn a suggestion into an intervention supposedly already performed. Clinical knowledge is not separately assessed in FaMed, but your wording must not distort the information.

## Practise two cases independently

Make separate notes for each practice case. After speaking, compare your recording with the supplied source: did you mix identities, times, findings or plans? Then repeat only the unclear section. Use the [differential-diagnosis phrasing exercise](/blog/differentialdiagnose-formulieren-deutsch) to practise degrees of certainty.

The [written station](/blog/famed-arztbrief-soap-schema) has a different task: anamnesis from its video in complete sentences. Do not carry this presentation's facts into it.

[See the real app workflow](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts) or [look inside the book](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau) to choose further practice material.

## Sources and review

Editorial check: **18 October 2026**, human medicine. [Official exam flow](https://famed-test.de/pruefungsablauf/), [Current human-medicine practice test](https://famed-test.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/FaMed-Uebungstest_2-1.pdf). Practice examples are created by FaMED Prep; they are not predictions of exam questions.

en.title: FaMED Written Task: The Anamnesis Section in 22 Minutes
en.excerpt: Write the anamnesis from a patient video in complete sentences; understand why a full SOAP note is the wrong target.
en.content:
The current human-medicine FaMed practice test asks for the **anamnesis section of a doctor's letter**, based on a patient video. The entire task has a **22-minute maximum, including video time**. The video may be paused and moved backward or forward.

## What belongs in the requested text

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

Capture the information actually given: identity and personal details, current symptoms and course, previous illnesses and medication, tobacco and alcohol use, family and social history and relevant travel history. Check the concrete assignment for the required information.

Write **complete sentences** using appropriate medical language. Convey patient statements with suitable distance, for example the Konjunktiv where appropriate. Do not turn missing information into a negative finding.

## Step 1: Extract facts before composing

Use a short note grid. Keep times, quantities and negations visible. Mark uncertain words so you can revisit the relevant video segment. A blank medication field does not mean the patient takes no medication.

For a fictional language exercise, suppose the source says:

> „Seit drei Tagen habe ich Bauchschmerzen. Mir ist übel, aber ich habe nicht erbrochen.“

Your notes could read: three days; abdominal pain; nausea; vomiting explicitly denied. They do not support a temperature, examination result or diagnosis.

## Step 2: Convert the notes into connected sentences

A possible formulation is:

> Der Patient gebe an, seit drei Tagen unter Bauchschmerzen zu leiden. Begleitend bestehe Übelkeit; Erbrechen werde verneint.

This is an original short example, not a complete model answer or an official case. Preserve the facts before trying to make the sentence more elaborate.

## Step 3: Check the draft against the source

Read for name and age, time course, side/location, units, medication names and negations. Then check sentence structure, verb forms, spelling and references. Use the 22-minute overall limit in full practice; your own viewing/writing split can change as you improve.

## Where SOAP does and does not help

SOAP organises some clinical notes into subjective, objective, assessment and plan. This FaMed assignment requests the anamnesis. It does **not** ask you to invent an objective examination, diagnosis, discharge plan or medication order to fill the other headings. Nor does it require you to recycle the patient from the earlier oral task.

For connected practice, read the [history-taking guide](/blog/anamnese-overview-part-1) and [terminology table](/blog/medizinische-fachbegriffe-laiensprache-tabelle). [See actual book pages](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau) for more phrasing practice, or [view the app workflow](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts).

## Sources and review

Editorial check: **18 October 2026**, human medicine. [Official exam flow](https://famed-test.de/pruefungsablauf/), [Current human-medicine practice test](https://famed-test.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/FaMed-Uebungstest_2-1.pdf). Practice examples are created by FaMED Prep; they are not predictions of exam questions.

en.title: FaMED Recognition: Check Your State and Qualification Route
en.excerpt: Find the authority conditions for your destination state and qualification route, with dated primary sources.
en.content:
Before booking FaMed, identify the authority responsible for your **human-medicine** licensing application. The exam centre's location does not determine whether that authority accepts the certificate.

The provider recognition overview remains labelled **November 2025**. Reading it in October 2026 does not turn it into a new 2026 policy. We distinguish provider statements from authority evidence below.

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

## What the primary sources support

| Destination | What to check |
|---|---|
| Rheinland-Pfalz | The LSJV authority page explicitly lists FaMed as a human-medicine FSP option. Check the rest of your application requirements. |
| Bayern | The provider lists general human-medicine acceptance. Current Bavarian authority pages direct foreign-qualification applications to Oberbayern/ZAABY. Check its current requirements; older Unterfranken FAQs are historical evidence, not current routing instructions. |
| Baden-Württemberg | Its authority currently names FaMed taken **after 13 May 2024**, provided the certificate accompanies the **initial application** and the exam is recognised in another state. A copy is sufficient for this proof. Later private certificates are not accepted under that procedure. |
| Hessen | Acceptance depends on the qualification route. The EU/EWR/Swiss authority leaflet names digiFORT, while associated documents are not fully consistent. Do not infer unconditional acceptance for every applicant or decide this by passport nationality. |
| Saarland, Thüringen, Sachsen-Anhalt | The provider's dated overview describes individual authority decisions. That is not a guarantee for a particular application. |
| Other states | This review does not establish acceptance or rejection. Use the responsible authority's current requirements. |

For detailed Baden-Württemberg conditions, use the [authority language FAQ](https://rp.baden-wuerttemberg.de/themen/bildung/ausbildung/seiten/faq-akad-heilberufe/sprachkenntnisse/). Its fee range for chamber examinations is not the FaMed fee.

## Ask about your actual application

Use the current provider/issuer name from your intended booking. Do not describe LMU as the organisation currently conducting your appointment.

A possible enquiry, where the authority accepts case enquiries:

> Ich beantrage die Approbation in der Humanmedizin. Mein Ausbildungsabschluss stammt aus [Land]; mein Aktenzeichen lautet [falls vorhanden]. Ich plane den Fachsprachennachweis über FaMed/digiFORT. Welche Voraussetzungen gelten in meinem Verfahren für Anerkennung, Prüfungsdatum, Aussteller und Zeitpunkt der Vorlage?

Attach or provide documents only through the authority's stated process. Some authorities do not answer hypothetical provider enquiries; read their published requirements first.

## Passing a language exam is not a licence

FaMed can satisfy an accepted language requirement. It does not itself grant **Approbation** or **Berufserlaubnis**. These are different permissions, and a Berufserlaubnis may carry restrictions.

Read [FaMED versus the Kenntnisprüfung](/blog/famed-vs-kenntnispruefung-kp) for the distinction between language and knowledge assessment. After checking your route, use the [preparation guide](/blog/ultimate-famed-preparation-guide) to organise learning. [See inside our book](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau) before choosing optional preparation material.

## Sources and review

Editorial check: **18 October 2026**, human medicine. [Provider overview, labelled November 2025](https://famed-test.de/ro/), [RLP authority](https://lsjv.rlp.de/themen/gesundheit/gesundheitsberufe/approbationen-fuer-akademische-heilberufe), [Bavaria: current foreign-qualification authority route](https://www.regierung.unterfranken.bayern.de/aufgaben/leistung/leistung_178578/index.html), [BW authority](https://rp.baden-wuerttemberg.de/themen/bildung/ausbildung/seiten/faq-akad-heilberufe/sprachkenntnisse/), [Hessen EU/EWR/Swiss leaflet](https://hlfgp.hessen.de/sites/hlfgp.hessen.de/files/2025-09/merkblatt_eu_medizin_1.pdf). Practice examples are created by FaMED Prep; they are not predictions of exam questions.

en.title: German Medical Terms in Everyday Language: A Practice Glossary
en.excerpt: Practise medical German explanations in everyday language. This is a study selection, not an official vocabulary list.
en.content:
These are language-practice examples. Select questions to fit the actual conversation and assignment; this is not an official mandatory checklist or a diagnostic rule-out tool. Medical knowledge is not separately assessed in FaMed, and cases can differ between tasks.

A patient may not understand a technical term even when it is medically familiar to you. Practise explaining it in everyday German and checking whether your explanation was understood.

Want to practise medical vocabulary in the context of a patient conversation? [Get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book) and work with its cases and useful phrases alongside this glossary.

For example, compare *"Wir müssen eine Cholezystektomie wegen einer Cholezystolithiasis durchführen"* with a more accessible explanation: *"Wir müssen die Gallenblase operativ entfernen, weil sich dort Gallensteine gebildet haben."*

Below is the practice glossary dividing clinical German into **Fachbegriff (Medical Term)** and **Laiensprache (Lay Translation)** across all major organ systems.

---

## 1. Cardiovascular & Respiratory Systems

## 6. Practical Exam Tip: The "Echo-Translation" Technique

When interacting with patients in the FaMED station, use the **Echo-Translation Technique**:

This demonstrates to examiners that you are conscious of communication barriers and actively safeguard patient clarity.

## A five-minute vocabulary exercise

en.title: After an Unsuccessful FaMED Attempt: Feedback and a Practical Retake Plan
en.excerpt: Use provider feedback to choose clear learning goals and build a practical retake preparation plan.
en.content:
An unsuccessful language-exam result can be discouraging. Start with the result and feedback available for the **specific examination you took**. FaMed and a chamber FSP may have different procedures.

## 1. Use the provider's feedback route

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

FaMed's current results page offers a free, binding **15-minute feedback video appointment** after an unsuccessful attempt. It describes a further appointment as possible no earlier than six months after the preceding feedback session. Check the booking details directly with the provider.

If you have a formal decision with review or appeal instructions, read those instructions promptly. This blog does not establish an appeal deadline or guarantee a particular legal entitlement to records.

A neutral request could be:

> Ich habe am [Datum] an der FaMed teilgenommen. Ich möchte das angebotene Nachgespräch nutzen. Bitte teilen Sie mir mit, wie ich einen Termin vereinbaren und welche Unterlagen ich dazu bereithalten kann.

## 2. Translate feedback into one observable goal

Examples: ask a clearer follow-up, keep two case presentations separate, preserve a negation from the video or explain a term in everyday language. Use actual feedback rather than guessing why a whole population fails.

Each of the three FaMed stations requires at least **60%**. Do not prepare on the assumption that a strong result in one can compensate for another below the limit.

## 3. Practise the current tasks

- History and informed consent share a 23-minute oral block including reading.
- Two patient presentations share another 23-minute block including reading.
- The written task is a 22-minute anamnesis section from a video, including viewing time.
- The current practice test sets an 11-minute maximum for each oral situation.

Use [the written-task guide](/blog/famed-arztbrief-soap-schema) rather than the former recommendation to write a full SOAP plan. Mnemonics should help you select relevant information, not force a fixed checklist into every conversation.

## 4. Plan the next weeks around evidence

Choose a schedule you can sustain. Review one attempt, work on one identified weakness, repeat the task, then compare the versions. Add full practice runs once individual skills are more reliable. Our [six-week plan](/blog/famed-vorbereitung-berufstaetig-6-wochen) is adaptable; six weeks is not a promise of readiness.

Check current repeat-booking and fee conditions with the provider before reserving another date. [See book excerpts](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau) and [the app demonstration](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts) before buying additional practice resources.

## Sources and review

[Results and feedback](https://famed-test.de/pruefungsergebnis/), [Exam flow](https://famed-test.de/pruefungsablauf/), [Practice test](https://famed-test.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/FaMed-Uebungstest_2-1.pdf). en.title: FaMED Symptom Questions: Clarify Important Information
en.excerpt: Practise focused questions and accurate reporting without invented automatic-failure rules or claims that a checklist rules out emergencies.
en.content:
Ask clear questions about the person's actual complaint, listen to the response and preserve important information.

FaMed assesses medical-language communication; medical knowledge is not separately evaluated. The following are original language exercises, not a complete emergency assessment or an official scoring checklist.

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

## Clarify the beginning and course

For a fictional pain-history exercise:

- „Wann haben die Beschwerden begonnen?“
- „Haben sie plötzlich eingesetzt oder allmählich zugenommen?“
- „Was war in diesem Moment anders als sonst?“

Use a clear follow-up when the answer is vague. „Seit gestern“ does not yet explain whether symptoms began suddenly or gradually.

## Ask one associated-symptom question at a time

Examples include „Haben Sie zusätzlich Atemnot bemerkt?“ or „Sind Sprach- oder Sehstörungen hinzugekommen?“. Choose according to the scenario rather than delivering an indiscriminate list.

Asking a question does not establish or rule out a diagnosis. Nor does the absence of one reported symptom justify saying that a serious condition is excluded.

## Distinguish a denial from missing information

These statements mean different things:

- „Die Patientin verneine Fieber.“ — she explicitly denied it.
- „Eine Temperaturmessung ist nicht angegeben.“ — no value was supplied.
- „Fieber wurde in dieser Übung nicht erfragt.“ — the question was not asked.

Do not write „B-Symptomatik verneint“ unless the relevant questions were actually answered. [The B-symptom article](/blog/b-symptoms-explained) shows how to ask about fever, sweating and weight change separately.

## Summarise without false reassurance

> Ich möchte kurz prüfen, ob ich Sie richtig verstanden habe: … Welche weitere Veränderung ist Ihnen aufgefallen?

If a practice scenario calls for an explanation of next steps, use its supplied plan. Do not invent a reassuring diagnosis or promise that a symptom is harmless.

For broader practice, use [the symptom-language checklist](/blog/anamnesis-red-flags-guide) and [pain questions](/blog/pain-anamnesis-guide). [See the app workflow](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts) or [look inside the book](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau) before selecting more exercises.

## Sources and review

en.title: FaMED and Kenntnisprüfung: Language Evidence and Medical Knowledge
en.excerpt: Understand how language assessment differs from the Kenntnisprüfung and why neither exam alone grants Approbation.
en.content:
**FaMed assesses professional German communication. The Kenntnisprüfung assesses medical knowledge and skills within a licensing procedure.** Passing either assessment does not, by itself, issue a medical licence.

Your responsible authority determines the route for your qualification and application. Do not assume every foreign-trained doctor must take a Kenntnisprüfung, or that document assessment always starts only after the language exam.

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

## Compare the purpose

| Question | FaMed | Kenntnisprüfung |
|---|---|---|
| What is assessed? | Professional medical German communication at C1 level | Medical knowledge and skills required by the applicable equivalence procedure |
| Typical task focus | Patient history, informed consent, two case presentations and written anamnesis | Oral-practical assessment with patient presentation under §37 ÄApprO |
| Who determines your eligibility and route? | Provider requirements and licensing-authority acceptance | The responsible licensing authority and examination procedure |
| Does passing automatically grant Approbation? | No | No; the authority must establish all requirements |

The official knowledge-test rules cover internal medicine and surgery, with additional aspects such as emergency medicine, pharmacotherapy, imaging, radiation protection and professional legal issues. They are not a promise of a particular set of elective questions. The old claim that the board must consist of three professors was too specific.

## Check equivalence and application requirements

A qualification may be recognised through the applicable recognition procedure; in other cases an authority can require a knowledge assessment. EU/EWR/Swiss and third-country routes must not be treated as identical. Use your authority's current instructions and any decision issued in your case.

A **Berufserlaubnis** is a separate permission that can have restrictions. Do not assume you can work while waiting merely because you passed FaMed or booked a Kenntnisprüfung.

For destination-state language requirements, read the [recognition guide](/blog/famed-anerkennung-bundeslaender-2026). For the current FaMed fee and live booking sources, use our [administrative guide](/blog/famed-kosten-termine-statistik-2026). No universal KP price or completion timeline is promised here.

## Transfer useful communication habits

Practice distinguishing patient-reported information, documented findings and your own interpretation. Use precise times, medication names and clear summaries. A framework such as SBAR can help you organise a practice presentation, but it is not a universal mandated answer structure for either assessment.

[Try the presentation exercise](/blog/sbar-schema-arzt-arzt-gespraech), then compare your answer with the actual assignment. [See the preparation app](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts) before deciding whether its available exercises suit your language goals.

en.title: The Digital FaMED Exam: Tasks, Video Notes and Typing Practice
en.excerpt: Prepare for the digital FaMed tasks: separate oral cases, video notes and the written anamnesis section.
en.content:
FaMed is a digital language examination taken **at a test centre**. It is not a remote exam you take from home. The provider's current FAQ lists Mainz, Kassel and Nürnberg; your confirmation supplies your appointment details.

## Understand the three stations

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

| Station | Tasks | Published block duration |
|---|---|---|
| Doctor–patient communication | History and informed consent | 23 minutes, including reading |
| Doctor–doctor communication | Two separate patient presentations | 23 minutes, including reading |
| Written communication | Anamnesis section based on a patient video | 22 minutes, including video |

The current practice test allows **at most 11 minutes per oral situation**. Do not confuse a situation with a whole paired station. Oral order can vary; writing is last, with one-minute station breaks. The cases need not follow one continuous patient story.

The published block durations do not establish a specific 30-second preparation screen or an exact reading-time subdivision.

## Prepare for the written video task

The current practice test permits pausing and moving forward or backward through the video. Take factual notes, check uncertain names, times and negations, then write the **anamnesis section in complete sentences**. Do not add an invented examination, diagnosis or treatment plan.

Our [written-task guide](/blog/famed-arztbrief-soap-schema) shows how to move from a source statement to a sentence. SOAP may be useful in other clinical documentation contexts, but it is not the required format of this FaMed task.

## Practise typing and clear audio

Practise German spelling, umlauts, punctuation and medical terms on a keyboard. Familiarity with a German layout can help; the exact equipment and instructions for your appointment come from the centre.

For speaking practice, make a test recording on your own device and listen for intelligibility. There is no requirement to adopt a particular pitch or a baritone voice.

In a timed writing practice, divide your available time between viewing, checking notes, composing and proofreading. Adjust those shares to the video and your typing speed. The overall official limit is not a universal minute-by-minute training script.

## Keep app practice distinct from the exam interface

FaMED Prep is an independent preparation app. [See its actual screens and workflow](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts); they do not prove what the official examination interface looks like. If you prefer a short daily exercise, use our [30-minute routine](/blog/famed-vorbereitung-30-minuten-lernroutine).

[Exam flow](https://famed-test.de/pruefungsablauf/), [Current practice test](https://famed-test.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/FaMed-Uebungstest_2-1.pdf), [FAQ](https://famed-test.de/faq/). Practice examples are created by FaMED Prep; they are not predictions of exam questions.

en.title: Diagnostic Uncertainty in German: Precise Phrases for Case Presentations
en.excerpt: Practise reporting a supplied suspicion, alternatives and missing information without inventing a clinical algorithm.
en.content:
In a medical-language presentation, precision is more useful than theatrical certainty. A suspected diagnosis is not a confirmed finding; an unanswered question is not a negative result.

FaMed supplies the information for its patient presentations and does not separately assess medical knowledge.

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

## Name the source and degree of certainty

Use the wording that the task supports:

| Information in the material | Possible German phrasing |
|---|---|
| Patient reports a symptom | „Die Patientin berichte über …“ |
| A finding is documented | „Im vorliegenden Befund wird … beschrieben.“ |
| A suspicion is stated | „Laut Aufgabeninformation besteht der Verdacht auf …“ |
| A diagnosis is confirmed in the source | „Als gesicherte Diagnose ist … angegeben.“ |
| Information is absent | „Hierzu liegen mir keine Angaben vor.“ |

These are practice formulations, not prescribed official sentences.

## Use alternatives without inventing a conclusion

If the assignment contains alternatives, introduce them clearly:

- „Als weitere Möglichkeit wird … genannt.“
- „Die Befunde erlauben laut Bericht noch keine eindeutige Zuordnung.“
- „Zur Klärung ist im vorgegebenen Plan … vorgesehen.“

If you offer an interpretation in a practice exercise, label it as your interpretation. Do not report that an investigation was performed or ordered when it was not.

## A fictional language exercise

Source note: a patient reports breathlessness after an operation; the supplied note describes a suspected embolism and planned further investigation. No result is given.

> Die Patientin berichte über nach einer Operation aufgetretene Atemnot. Im vorliegenden Bericht wird der Verdacht auf eine Lungenembolie genannt. Die weitere Abklärung sei geplant; ein Untersuchungsergebnis liegt in dieser Übung nicht vor.

This exercise practises source accuracy, not the clinical diagnosis or exclusion of embolism.

## Keep connectors proportionate

„Dafür spricht …“ indicates supporting information; it does not mean „beweist …“. „Dagegen spricht …“ does not automatically mean „sicher ausgeschlossen“. Practise that difference using only the facts provided.

Use [SBAR as an organising aid](/blog/sbar-schema-arzt-arzt-gespraech), then compare the recorded presentation with its source. For patient-facing questions, see [the history guide](/blog/anamnese-overview-part-1).

[Our book preview](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau) and [app walkthrough](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts) show independent resources for further practice.

en.title: FaMED Preparation While Working: An Adaptable Six-Week Plan
en.excerpt: Fit speaking, source-based writing and review around work, with realistic task timings and no promised completion date.
en.content:
Preparing while working requires a schedule you can repeat. Six weeks is an example planning window, not evidence that every learner can reach the required language level in that time. Begin by checking the current task requirements and your own baseline.

## A possible 90-minute study session

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

Use three flexible blocks: vocabulary in context, one speaking exercise, then writing or review. Ninety minutes is a study suggestion, not an official requirement.

For speaking, distinguish a single oral situation from a whole station: the current practice test gives at most 11 minutes per situation; the two paired oral blocks are each 23 minutes including reading. For writing, practise the 22-minute task including video time.

The written output is the **anamnesis section from its video**, not a full SOAP letter derived from your preceding spoken case. [See the writing method](/blog/famed-arztbrief-soap-schema).

## Weeks 1–2: Understand and clarify

Practise opening a history, asking one clear follow-up and summarising what the person actually said. Use varied fictional symptoms and relevant background questions. Keep short writing sessions in the plan from the beginning.

A limited-time day can use our [30-minute routine](/blog/famed-vorbereitung-30-minuten-lernroutine). Mark any unresolved language point for the next session.

## Weeks 3–4: Explain and present

Use supplied procedure notes for informed-consent practice. Explain the information without invented risk frequencies, guaranteed outcomes or unsupported aftercare rules.

For patient presentations, keep two fictional cases separate. Report the supplied history, findings and plan accurately, then practise short answers to follow-up questions. This is a language task, not a medical-knowledge interrogation.

[Read the consent guide](/blog/famed-aufklaerungsgespraech-guide) and the [presentation framework](/blog/sbar-schema-arzt-arzt-gespraech) for concrete exercises.

## Weeks 5–6: Timing, feedback and repetition

Use the provider's current practice test. Compare each attempt with the source, then repeat a specific weak section. Build toward complete task sequences and allow time for feedback. If your baseline needs longer, extend the schedule rather than treating the calendar as a deadline for readiness.

In each week, practise spelling and keyboard familiarity, listening to names and quantities, and distinguishing missing information from explicitly denied symptoms.

## Learn appropriately at work

Follow your workplace's access, supervision and confidentiality rules. Use only authorised teaching examples and materials. Do not access patient records simply for private exam preparation, and do not upload or record identifiable patient information in a study app.

Notice useful ways colleagues structure explanations, then create a fictional example in your own words. Patient care is not a private mock-exam session.

[See actual book pages](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau) or [read the app walkthrough](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts) before adding optional resources. [The eight-week plan](/blog/8-week-famed-study-plan) offers a longer template.

Practice examples are created by FaMED Prep; they are not predictions of exam questions.

en.title: 15 German Patient Expressions: Ask What They Mean
en.excerpt: German patients rarely speak in textbook German. Practise 15 everyday expressions and clarify what the person means. These are examples, not an official exam list.
en.content:
These are language-practice examples. Select questions to fit the actual conversation and assignment; this is not an official mandatory checklist or a diagnostic rule-out tool. Medical knowledge is not separately assessed in FaMed, and cases can differ between tasks.

You have passed your B2/C1 Goethe or telc exam, memorized medical anatomy in German, and practiced your questions. But then you enter your FaMED examination room, and the patient actor says:

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

> *"Herr Doktor, mir ist ganz flau im Magen und gestern hatte ich wieder diesen Kloß im Hals. Außerdem hab ich's total im Kreuz!"*

If you pause with a blank look or ask the patient to repeat themselves in high academic German, ask a clear follow-up rather than guessing the meaning.

German patients use rich colloquial idioms (*Umgangssprache*) to describe physical suffering. Below are the **Top 15 everyday idioms** for language practice, possible descriptions, and how to clarify them professionally.

---


---

## The 15 Essential Patient Idioms

### 1. "Ich hab's im Kreuz."
* **Literal Meaning:** I have it in the cross.
* **Possible description:** Back or lower-back discomfort; severity and radiation need clarification.
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Wo genau tut es Ihnen weh? Strahlt der Schmerz über das Gesäß in ein Bein aus?"*

### 2. "Mir ist ganz flau im Magen."
* **Literal Meaning:** It is lukewarm/weak in my stomach.
* **Possible description:** Queasiness, mild nausea, or pre-syncopal lightheadedness.
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Fühlt sich das wie Übelkeit an, oder wird Ihnen dabei auch schwindelig und schwarz vor Augen?"*

### 3. "Ich habe einen Kloß im Hals."
* **Literal Meaning:** I have a dumpling in my throat.
* **Possible description:** Globus sensation, dysphagia, or emotional choking sensation (*Globus pharyngis*).
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Haben Sie echte Schwierigkeiten beim Schlucken fester Nahrung, oder fühlt es sich eher wie ein Engegefühl an?"*

### 4. "Das schlägt mir auf das Gemüt."
* **Literal Meaning:** It hits my mind/soul.
* **Possible description:** Something affecting the person’s mood; not a diagnosis of depression.
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Fühlen Sie sich in letzter Zeit niedergeschlagen, antriebslos oder traurig?"*

### 5. "Ich habe Wasser in den Beinen."
* **Literal Meaning:** I have water in my legs.
* **Possible description:** Peripheral edema / pitting edema (*Periphere Ödeme bei Herzinsuffizienz oder CVI*).
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Bemerken Sie, dass Ihre Socken am Abend tiefe Abdrücke an den Knöcheln hinterlassen?"*

### 6. "Mir schwirrt der Kopf." / "Mir dreht sich alles."
* **Literal Meaning:** My head is buzzing / everything is spinning.
* **Possible description:** Vertigo or dizziness (*Drehschwindel oder Benommenheit*).
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Fühlt sich der Schwindel wie Karussellfahren an, oder ist es eher ein Gefühl von Unsicherheit beim Gehen?"*

### 7. "Ich kriege keine Luft mehr."
* **Literal Meaning:** I can't get any air anymore.
* **Possible description:** Acute or exertional dyspnea (*Atemnot*).
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Tritt die Atemnot in Ruhe auf oder nur bei körperlicher Anstrengung, beispielsweise beim Treppensteigen?"*

### 8. "Mein Magen brennt wie Feuer."
* **Literal Meaning:** My stomach burns like fire.
* **Possible description:** Pyrosis, heartburn, or acid reflux (*Sodbrennen / Refluxösophagitis*).
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Steigt dieser brennende Schmerz hinter dem Brustbein nach oben in den Hals auf, besonders nach dem Essen oder im Liegen?"*

### 9. "Ich bin fix und fertig." / "Ich fühle mich wie gerädert."
* **Literal Meaning:** I am fixed and finished / like broken on a wheel.
* **Possible description:** Fatigue or exhaustion; the expression alone does not establish sleep apnea (*Chronische Erschöpfung / Fatigue*).
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Fühlen Sie sich morgens nach dem Aufwachen unerholt, oder schnarchen Sie nachts?"*

### 10. "Ich habe mir den Magen verdorben."
* **Literal Meaning:** I have spoiled my stomach.
* **Possible description:** The person attributes stomach or digestive discomfort to something they ate; clarify rather than assuming an infection.
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Haben Sie etwas Ungewöhnliches gegessen, und leiden Sie unter Durchfall oder Erbrechen?"*

### 11. "Das Herz klopft mir bis zum Hals."
* **Literal Meaning:** My heart is pounding up to my throat.
* **Possible description:** Palpitations / tachycardia (*Palpitationen / Tachykardie*).
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Schlägt das Herz dabei ganz regelmäßig oder stolpert es unregelmäßig?"*

### 12. "Ich habe Stiche in der Brust."
* **Literal Meaning:** I have needle pricks in the chest.
* **Possible description:** Stabbing chest discomfort; whether it relates to breathing needs clarification (*Stechender, atemabhängiger Thoraxschmerz*).
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Werden die Stiche stärker, wenn Sie tief einatmen oder husten?"*

### 13. "Ich habe einen Frosch im Hals."
* **Literal Meaning:** I have a frog in my throat.
* **Possible description:** Hoarseness, tickle in throat, need to clear throat (*Heiserkeit / Räusperzwang*).
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Seit wann besteht die Heiserkeit und müssen Sie sich ständig räuspern?"*

### 14. "Mir ist eine Laus über die Leber gelaufen."
* **Literal Meaning:** A louse ran across my liver.
* **Possible description:** Irritable, bad-tempered, angry (*Gereiztheit / Dysphorie*).
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Gibt es einen bestimmten Grund, der Sie heute besonders verärgert oder belastet hat?"*

### 15. "Das Bein ist pelzig."
* **Literal Meaning:** The leg feels like fur.
* **Possible description:** Numbness, hypoesthesia, paresthesia (*Taubheitsgefühl / Parästhesie*).
* **Doctor's Follow-up:** *"Fühlt sich die Haut taub an wie eingeschlafen, oder kribbelt es wie tausend Ameisen?"*

---


For a practical next step, continue with [German Medical Terms in Everyday Language: A Practice Glossary](/blog/medizinische-fachbegriffe-laiensprache-tabelle).

## The Rule for Clarifying Patient Idioms

Whenever a patient uses an idiom you are not 100% sure about, **never guess**. Echo the symptom back in a clarifying question:

> *"Wenn Sie sagen, 'es sticht wie ein Messer', bedeutet das, der Schmerz ist plötzlich und schneidend eingeschossen?"*

Examiners reward active clarification as a sign of excellent clinical communication.

---


To build on this exercise, read [Mastering the FaMED Anamnese: Part 1 - Overview & Key Strategies](/blog/anamnese-overview-part-1).


Want to turn your reading into practice? [See how the FaMED Prep app works, step by step](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts), before deciding whether its exercises fit your preparation.

en.title: Cardiology Language Practice: Symptoms, Findings and Case Presentations
en.excerpt: Practise accurate German communication with fictional cardiovascular examples, without invented exam frequencies or treatment algorithms.
en.content:
Cardiovascular examples can help you practise medical German. They are not evidence that a particular diagnosis appears in a certain share of FaMed exams.

FaMed assesses language performance, not medical knowledge separately. In the presentation task, report the information supplied rather than inventing a diagnosis, drug dose or intervention.

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

## Ask about a reported symptom

For a fictional history exercise involving chest discomfort, practise clear questions:

- „Seit wann bestehen die Beschwerden?“
- „Wie fühlen sie sich an, und wo genau spüren Sie sie?“
- „Strahlen die Beschwerden aus?“
- „Was hat sich seit Beginn verändert?“

These examples practise language. Answers alone do not confirm or exclude a particular disease. Use the [pain-history framework](/blog/pain-anamnesis-guide) to adapt follow-up questions to the source scenario.

## Separate the patient's report from findings

Suppose a fictional source states that Herr Beispiel reports breathlessness when lying down, that his legs have become swollen, and that an examination report is not supplied.

A faithful formulation is:

> Herr Beispiel berichte über Atemnot im Liegen und neu aufgetretene Beinschwellungen. Zu Auskultation und Vitalparametern liegen im vorliegenden Material keine Angaben vor.

Do not add crackles, oxygen saturation or a medication administration simply because they might fit an expected diagnosis.

## Present a documented finding precisely

If the source actually supplies an ECG finding, measurement or plan, report it with its units, timing and context. Preserve whether the source calls something suspected or confirmed. An assessment must not become more certain merely to make your language sound confident.

[The SBAR practice article](/blog/sbar-schema-arzt-arzt-gespraech) helps organise information. It does not prescribe a compulsory official schema or clinical treatment sequence.

## Use the correct task for writing

The written station asks for the anamnesis section from its video. It does not require you to write an acute-heart-failure treatment plan or carry over this cardiology case. See the [written-task guide](/blog/famed-arztbrief-soap-schema).

For further independent language practice, [look inside the digital book](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau) or [see the app's real exercise areas](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts). This article contains no treatment protocol or prediction of official exam cases.

## Sources and review

[Official exam flow](https://famed-test.de/pruefungsablauf/), [Current human-medicine practice test](https://famed-test.de/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/FaMed-Uebungstest_2-1.pdf). Practice examples are created by FaMED Prep; they are not predictions of exam questions.

en.title: Abdominal Pain in FaMED Practice: Questions and Clear Reporting
en.excerpt: Use fictional abdominal examples to practise questions, source distinctions and patient-friendly language.
en.content:
Abdominal complaints are useful material for medical-language practice. In FaMed, the task is not a practical surgical examination or a test of whether you know when to operate. Medical knowledge is not separately assessed.

## Clarify the complaint in everyday German

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

Begin with an open question, then follow the reported symptom:

- „Wo genau haben Sie Schmerzen?“
- „Wo haben die Schmerzen begonnen? Hat sich der Ort verändert?“
- „Seit wann bestehen die Beschwerden, und wie haben sie sich entwickelt?“
- „Welche weiteren Beschwerden haben Sie bemerkt?“

Use [OPQRST](/blog/pain-anamnesis-guide) as a flexible memory aid. Select relevant questions rather than making every patient complete the same checklist.

## Do not turn a symptom into a confirmed diagnosis

A fictional source might report pain that moved from the middle of the abdomen to the right lower abdomen. You can accurately describe that movement without asserting that it proves appendicitis.

> Der Patient gebe an, die Schmerzen hätten zunächst im mittleren Bauchbereich begonnen und seien später in den rechten Unterbauch gewandert.

A reported symptom is different from an examination finding. Do not say you palpated the abdomen when no examination took place in the task.

## Report supplied findings separately

If a presentation sheet contains an examination report, use wording such as „Laut Untersuchungsbericht …“. If a finding or plan is absent, say so. Avoid filling gaps with a textbook pattern.

For example:

> Zu den Laborwerten liegen mir in diesem Material keine Angaben vor.

[The presentation guide](/blog/sbar-schema-arzt-arzt-gespraech) shows how to organise the available information. [The differential-phrasing article](/blog/differentialdiagnose-formulieren-deutsch) helps mark a suspicion without presenting it as confirmed.

## Explain the supplied procedure, not an invented continuation

The informed-consent task may involve a different patient and procedure. Use its information about purpose, sequence, risks and perioperative behaviour. Do not assume the abdominal history automatically leads to a specific operation.

The [consent guide](/blog/famed-aufklaerungsgespraech-guide) gives adaptable language patterns. [See the book preview](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau) for independent phrasing material. No diagnosis frequency or clinical treatment pathway is claimed here.

en.title: FaMED Exam Fee, Booking and Results: What Is Verified in 2026
en.excerpt: The published €530 exam fee, current booking sources, result timing and a practical planning checklist.
en.content:
The official FaMed FAQ currently lists the human-medicine exam fee as **€530**. This is the exam provider's fee, separate from any FaMED Prep book or app purchase. Check the amount and conditions in the official booking before paying.

## Build your own budget

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

Start with the exam fee, then request actual prices for any travel, accommodation, translations, language certificates and preparation resources you need. These costs differ by person. There is no verified all-inclusive budget here, and we cannot promise that every expense is tax-deductible.

The FAQ lists **Mainz, Kassel and Nürnberg**. Check the address in your booking confirmation. Do not assume another city is a current exam centre because an old article names it.

Our digital book offer is **€19.99**. [Look at real book pages first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau). Preparation purchases are optional and do not reserve an official exam place.

## Book against live availability

Use the [official booking page](https://famed-test.de/buchungsseite/). No universal six-to-eight-week registration window, monthly testing frequency or guaranteed waiting period was verified. Choose a real available date and read the conditions for that booking.

The provider's FAQ requires a B2 certificate upload for Rheinland-Pfalz registration. This does not establish an identical upload rule for every route. First check [recognition in your destination state](/blog/famed-anerkennung-bundeslaender-2026) and the documents required by your authority.

## Results and passing requirements

The results page gives a usual processing period of **two to four weeks**; the FAQ says approximately four weeks. Treat this as guidance, not a guaranteed delivery date. Results arrive by email, with a successful digital certificate sent separately.

Each of the three stations requires **at least 60%**. A stronger station cannot compensate for one below that threshold.

We have not verified a public cohort dataset supporting a first-attempt pass rate, a retake percentage or a claimed success rate for our preparation materials. A personal result cannot be predicted from an invented statistic.

## Check cancellation terms before paying

The provider FAQ contains conflicting cancellation-fee figures. Follow the current terms attached to your booking and obtain clarification from the provider where they conflict. Do not budget using an old blog's cancellation amount.

Once the administrative steps are clear, adapt our [six-week preparation plan](/blog/famed-vorbereitung-berufstaetig-6-wochen) to your needs. [Request the free study guide](/lead-magnet) if you need a starting schedule.

en.title: Systematic Anamnesis for Sore Throat, Chronic Fatigue & Infectious Symptoms
en.excerpt: Master structured German anamnesis for patients presenting with sore throat, chronic fatigue, and infectious signs in the FaMED exam.
en.content:
These are language-practice examples. Select questions to fit the actual conversation and assignment; this is not an official mandatory checklist or a diagnostic rule-out tool. Medical knowledge is not separately assessed in FaMed, and cases can differ between tasks.

## Introduction

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

The systematic Anamnese is a cornerstone of medical diagnostics. It allows the doctor to gain a comprehensive picture of the patient and their complaints in order to make an informed diagnosis and develop an appropriate treatment plan. This blog post focuses on structured history-taking for patients with sore throat, chronic fatigue, and/or infectious symptoms, giving you a solid framework for the FaMED exam.


For a practical next step, continue with [B-Symptoms Explained: Your Guide to Weight Loss, Fever & Night Sweats](/blog/b-symptoms-explained).

## Systematic Anamnese

### 1. Introduction and Greeting

Start the conversation with a friendly greeting and introduce yourself. Explain your role and the purpose of the conversation. Make sure the patient consents to the history-taking and has room for questions.

*   **Example:** "Guten Tag, mein Name ist [Ihr Name]. Ich bin Assistenzarzt/Ärztin hier im Krankenhaus und möchte gerne ein Aufnahmegespräch mit Ihnen führen. Sind Sie damit einverstanden? Wenn Sie Fragen haben, sagen Sie es mir bitte jederzeit."

### 2. Personal Data (Persönliche Daten)

Collect the patient's basic personal data.

*   **Questions:**
*   Wie heißen Sie?
*   Wann sind Sie geboren?
*   Wie alt sind Sie?
*   Wie groß sind Sie?
*   Wie viel wiegen Sie?

### 3. Current History (Aktuelle Anamnese)

Determine the main reason for the visit and the patient's primary complaints. Let the patient tell their story.

*   **Questions:**
*   Was führt Sie zu uns?
*   Warum sind Sie ins Krankenhaus gekommen?
*   Was kann ich für Sie tun, Herr/Frau …?

### 4. General Complaints (Allgemeine Beschwerden)

Ask about current complaints in detail.

*   **Questions:**
*   Was für Beschwerden haben Sie?
*   Seit wann haben Sie diese Beschwerden?
*   Hatten Sie einen Unfall?
*   Haben Sie das Bewusstsein verloren? War Ihnen schwindelig oder schwarz vor Augen?
*   Hatten Sie diese Beschwerden früher schon einmal?
*   Verändern sich die Beschwerden im Laufe der Zeit?
*   Haben Sie noch weitere Beschwerden? Ist Ihnen noch etwas aufgefallen?
*   Haben Sie etwas Ungewöhnliches bemerkt?

### 5. Pain Analysis (Schmerzanalyse) — if applicable

If the patient has pain, conduct a detailed pain analysis. Use the OPQRST framework.

*   **Timing (Zeitliches Auftreten):**
*   Seit wann haben Sie Schmerzen?
*   Haben die Schmerzen plötzlich begonnen oder langsam?
*   Wie lange dauert der Schmerz an?
*   Ist der Schmerz dauerhaft oder sind Sie manchmal auch schmerzfrei?
*   **Location (Lokalisation):**
*   Wo genau tut es Ihnen weh?
*   Strahlen die Schmerzen aus?
*   **Severity (Stärke):**
*   Wie stark sind die Schmerzen auf einer Skala von 0-10, wobei 0 kein Schmerz und 10 der stärkste vorstellbare Schmerz ist?
*   **Quality (Qualität):**
*   Wie fühlen sich die Schmerzen an? Sind sie eher brennend, drückend, stechend, klopfend, ziehend, …?
*   **Triggers/Relief (Auslöser/Linderung):**
*   Können Sie einen Auslöser für die Schmerzen erkennen?
*   Haben Sie die Beschwerden nur bei Belastung oder auch in Ruhe?
*   Gibt es etwas, das die Schmerzen lindert/verstärkt?
*   Hilft Ihnen eher Wärme oder Kälte?
*   **Medication (Einnahme von Medikamenten):**
*   Haben Sie etwas gegen die Schmerzen eingenommen? Hat es geholfen?

### 6. Vegetative History (Vegetative Anamnese)

Ask about relevant general symptoms without assuming a specific cause.

*   **Questions:**
*   War Ihnen übel? Mussten Sie erbrechen? Leiden Sie unter Übelkeit oder Erbrechen?
*   Haben Sie Nachtschweiß bemerkt?
*   Haben Sie Fieber gemessen?
*   Haben Sie Probleme beim Wasserlassen oder Stuhlgang? Leiden Sie unter Durchfall oder Verstopfung?
*   Schlafen Sie gut? Haben Sie Ein- oder Durchschlafschwierigkeiten?
*   Hat sich Ihr Appetit in letzter Zeit verändert?
*   Haben Sie in letzter Zeit ungewollt zu- oder abgenommen?
*   Haben Sie Husten? Kommt dabei Schleim hoch oder ist es ein trockener Husten?

### 7. Gynecological History (Gynäkologische Anamnese) — where relevant

Ask reproductive-history questions where relevant to the person, symptoms and assignment; do not apply every question to every conversation.

*   **Questions:**
*   Wie sieht es mit Ihrer Menstruation aus? Haben Sie sie noch? Ist sie regelmäßig?
*   Wann hatten Sie Ihre letzte Regelblutung?
*   Haben Sie Menstruationsbeschwerden?
*   Waren Sie schon einmal schwanger? Haben Sie Kinder?
*   Besteht im Moment die Möglichkeit einer Schwangerschaft?
*   Verhüten Sie? Wie verhüten Sie?

### 8. Previous Illnesses / Surgeries (Vorerkrankungen / Voroperationen)

Ask about relevant previous illnesses and surgeries.

*   **Questions:**
*   Leiden Sie an chronischen Erkrankungen? (z.B. Diabetes, Bluthochdruck)
*   Waren Sie in letzter Zeit im Krankenhaus oder in ärztlicher Behandlung?
*   Sind Sie schon einmal operiert worden? Wann? Aus welchem Grund?

### 9. Medications (Medikamente)

Record the patient's current medication.

*   **Questions:**
*   Nehmen Sie regelmäßig Medikamente ein?
*   In welcher Dosierung?
*   Nehmen Sie etwas bei Bedarf ein?
*   Hat Ihnen das Medikament geholfen?

### 10. Allergies (Allergien)

Ask about known allergies and intolerances.

*   **Questions:**
*   Sind bei Ihnen Allergien oder Unverträglichkeiten bekannt?
*   Haben Sie Lebensmittelunverträglichkeiten (z.B. Laktoseintoleranz)?
*   Wogegen sind Sie allergisch?
*   Wie äußert sich diese Allergie / Unverträglichkeit?
*   Nehmen Sie Medikamente gegen die Allergie?

### 11. Substance Use (Noxen)

Ask about tobacco, alcohol, and drug use.

*   **Questions:**
*   Rauchen Sie? Haben Sie jemals geraucht? Seit wann rauchen Sie? Wie viele Zigaretten rauchen sie am Tag / in der Woche?
*   Trinken Sie (regelmäßig) Alkohol? Wie häufig und wie viel trinken Sie ungefähr?
*   Hatten Sie schon einmal Kontakt mit Drogen?

### 12. Family History (Familienanamnese)

Ask about relevant diseases in the family.

*   **Questions:**
*   Sind Ihre Eltern gesund? Woran sind sie gestorben?
*   Sind Ihre Geschwister gesund?
*   Hat jemand in Ihrer Familie ähnliche Beschwerden wie Sie?
*   Gibt es Erbkrankheiten in Ihrer Familie? Gibt es in Ihrer Familie chronische Erkrankungen oder Vorerkrankungen, von denen ich wissen sollte, zum Beispiel Diabetes, Krebs oder Herz-Kreislauf-Erkrankungen?

### 13. Psychological History (Psychoanamnese)

Ask about psychological burdens and stressors.

*   **Questions:**
*   Haben Sie in letzter Zeit vermehrt Stress oder etwas, das Sie mental belastet?
*   Fühlen Sie sich in letzter Zeit stark belastet oder gestresst?

### 14. Social History (Sozialanamnese)

Ask about professional and social circumstances.

*   **Questions:**
*   Was machen Sie beruflich?
*   Haben Sie Stress bei der Arbeit?
*   Sind Sie verheiratet? Haben Sie Kinder?
*   Leben Sie allein? Mit wem leben Sie zusammen?

### 15. Specific Questions (Based on Symptoms)

#### **Sore throat / Tonsillitis (Halsschmerzen / Mandelentzündung):**

*   Wie stark sind die Schmerzen (Skala 1-10)?
*   Wie fühlen sich die Schmerzen an (stechend, drückend, pulsierend)?
*   Haben Sie Husten, Schluckbeschwerden oder ein Kratzen im Hals?
*   Sind Ihre Lymphknoten am Hals geschwollen und schmerzhaft?
*   Haben Sie Veränderungen im Mund bemerkt (z.B. an der Schleimhaut)?
*   Ist Ihre Stimme verändert?
*   Hatten Sie kürzlich Kontakt zu jemandem mit ähnlichen Symptomen?
*   Waren Sie in letzter Zeit in großen Menschenmengen?

#### **Chronic Fatigue (Chronische Müdigkeit / Fatigue):**

*   Seit wann fühlen Sie sich erschöpft oder müde?
*   Sind die Beschwerden ständig da oder kommen sie nur manchmal mit Pausen?
*   Hat sich die Erschöpfung im Laufe der Zeit verändert (besser oder schlimmer geworden)?
*   Gibt es etwas, das die Beschwerden verbessert oder verschlechtert (Ruhe, Schlaf, Aktivität, Ernährung)?
*   Haben Sie selbst etwas dagegen unternommen (Medikamente, mehr Schlaf, Bewegung, Nahrungsergänzungsmittel)?
*   Haben Sie in letzter Zeit Erkältungssymptome wie Fieber oder Nachtschweiß bemerkt?
*   Hat sich Ihr Appetit in letzter Zeit verändert?
*   Haben Sie Schwierigkeiten, einzuschlafen oder durchzuschlafen?

#### **Infectious Symptoms (COVID, Flu, etc.):**

*   Seit wann haben Sie die Beschwerden?
*   Wie haben die Beschwerden begonnen (plötzlich oder langsam)?
*   Haben sich die Beschwerden verändert (besser oder schlimmer geworden)?
*   Haben Sie einen COVID-Test gemacht? Wie war das Ergebnis?
*   Haben Sie weitere Symptome bemerkt, zum Beispiel Fieber oder Husten?
*   Hatten Sie in letzter Zeit Kontakt mit einer erkälteten oder positiv getesteten Person?
*   Sind Sie gegen COVID-19 geimpft?
*   Haben Sie selbst etwas gegen die Beschwerden unternommen (Medikamente, Hausmittel, Arztbesuch)?

### 16. Closing the Conversation (Gesprächsabschluss)

Summarize the key information and give the patient the opportunity to add anything. Explain the next steps supported by the actual assignment; the following is a fictional language example, not a universal investigation plan.

*   **Example:** "Jetzt würde ich noch einmal kurz zusammenfassen: Sie haben … Habe ich alles richtig verstanden? Möchten Sie noch etwas hinzufügen? Als Nächstes werde ich eine körperliche Untersuchung durchführen, Ihre Lunge und Ihr Herz abhören sowie Ihren Bauch abtasten. Außerdem werde ich Ihnen ein bisschen Blut abnehmen, um die Blutwerte zu kontrollieren. Die weiteren Schritte richten sich nach den erhobenen Informationen und der vorgesehenen Abklärung. Haben Sie noch Fragen an mich? Dann gehen wir weiter."


## Conclusion

A structured and systematic Anamnese is essential for diagnosis. By consistently covering all relevant areas, you can find the right direction even with complex symptom patterns such as chronic fatigue, sore throat, or unclear infectious symptoms.


To build on this exercise, read [Mastering the FaMED Anamnese: Part 1 - Overview & Key Strategies](/blog/anamnese-overview-part-1).


Want to turn your reading into practice? [See how the FaMED Prep app works, step by step](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts), before deciding whether its exercises fit your preparation.

en.title: B-Symptoms in German: Ask About Fever, Sweating and Weight Change
en.excerpt: Understand the term and practise source-faithful questions without diagnosing cancer from a symptom list.
en.content:
The term **B-symptoms** is used particularly in lymphoma contexts for unexplained fever above 38°C, marked night sweats and unintended weight loss of more than 10% over six months. These symptoms can have different causes; they do not by themselves diagnose cancer or establish its stage.

This article focuses on German questions and documentation. It is not a fixed investigation plan.

For cases and useful phrases to practise alongside this topic, [get the FaMED Protokoll digital book for €19.99](https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/DQCLR47JB5DXU?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contextual_book). You can also [read a sample first](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau).

## Ask about each symptom separately

For weight change:

> Haben Sie ungewollt Gewicht verloren? Wie viel ungefähr und in welchem Zeitraum? Wie hoch war Ihr Gewicht vorher?

For fever:

> Haben Sie Fieber gemessen? Wie hoch war die Temperatur, und wann wurde sie gemessen?

For night sweating:

> Schwitzen Sie nachts? Ist es so stark, dass Sie Kleidung oder Bettwäsche wechseln müssen? Wie oft kommt das vor?

One answer does not establish that the other symptoms were denied. Avoid writing a blanket „B-Symptomatik verneint“ after asking only about weight.

## Keep the report faithful

Fictional source statement: „Ich habe in drei Monaten etwa vier Kilo verloren, ohne eine Diät zu machen.“

Possible formulation:

> Der Patient gebe an, innerhalb von drei Monaten ungewollt etwa vier Kilogramm abgenommen zu haben.

Without the starting weight you cannot infer a percentage. Do not change „etwa“ into an exact measurement. If no fever question was asked, do not add „afebril“.

## Respond to concern honestly

A useful response acknowledges the question without guaranteeing a diagnosis:

> Ich verstehe, dass Sie sich Sorgen machen. Diese Beschwerden können unterschiedliche Ursachen haben. Wir halten zunächst genau fest, was sich verändert hat, und besprechen die vorgesehenen nächsten Schritte.

Avoid „Krebs ist ausgeschlossen“ or a claim about inheritance when the available information does not support it. Clinical investigations depend on professional assessment in the actual case.

## Put the questions into a conversation

FaMed assesses language performance, not a memorised oncology algorithm. Ask relevant questions, listen and summarise. The [oncological-history examples](/blog/oncological-anamnesis-mastery) and [general history guide](/blog/anamnese-overview-part-1) show how these information groups fit into a conversation.

[See our digital book sample](/blog/famed-protokoll-buch-vorschau) or [view the app walkthrough](/blog/famed-prep-app-so-funktionierts) for further language practice.

## Sources and review
